new_jobs.title: College Corps Program Coordinator - San Francisco State University
new_jobs.description:
Another Source’s client, San Francisco State University
, is recruiting a College Corps Coordinator
to join their team in San Francisco, California.

First and foremost, this position requires someone with a strong work ethic. The work is fast-paced and involves the ability to adapt to changing priorities but is also immensely fulling and fun.
This position requires onsite presence on campus 5 days/week but allows for a flexible schedule to attend exciting events to get the word out about the program! Relocation assistance is not available.

Here’s a little about San Francisco State University and the Institute for Civic & Community Engagement:

San Francisco State University’s Institute for Civic & Community Engagement (ICCE) connects students, faculty, and community partners through civic engagement, experiential learning, and community-based programs. Within ICCE, California College Corps creates opportunities for students to serve their communities while developing leadership skills, professional experience, and a deeper connection to civic life.

The College Corps Coordinator plays a hands-on role in making that experience possible. From recruiting and supporting Fellows to building strong community partnerships and keeping a complex state- and federally funded program running smoothly, this position combines student engagement, program administration, community partnership development, events, communications, and grant compliance.

About this role:

Reporting to the Executive Director, the College Corps Coordinator will manage an assigned portfolio of Fellows and community partners while working collaboratively with other College Corps Coordinators as a cross-trained member of the team.

This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys variety and wants their work to have a direct impact on students and the broader community. You’ll guide Fellows throughout their College Corps experience, build relationships with community organizations, coordinate engaging educational programming, and help ensure the program meets university, California Volunteers, AmeriCorps, and grant requirements.

Your Contribution Will Likely Include

Program Coordination & Fellow Engagement – 30%

Coordinate the full Fellow experience, from recruitment, application review, and selection through onboarding, placement, participation, completion, and program exit.
Serve as a primary resource for an assigned portfolio of Fellows, helping them navigate program expectations, deadlines, resources, and requirements.
Monitor service hours, attendance, eligibility, participation, and program milestones while proactively identifying barriers to successful participation.
Design and facilitate orientations, Team Circles, professional development workshops, leadership activities, reflection sessions, and other educational programming.
Create opportunities that strengthen Fellows’ civic engagement, career readiness, leadership development, and professional skills.
Coordinate Fellow participation in campus events, service projects, conferences, outreach activities, recognition events, and graduation celebrations.

Community Partnership Development & Engagement – 20%

Build and manage relationships with an assigned portfolio of community partner organizations.
Recruit, onboard, and support community partners and Fellowship Supervisors throughout the academic year.
Coordinate partnership agreements, position descriptions, placement processes, evaluations, and site visits.
Provide partners with guidance on program expectations, student supervision, compliance requirements, and best practices.
Support ICCE initiatives such as community-based service programs, food security efforts, volunteer engagement, and other experiential learning opportunities.

Program Administration, Compliance & Fiscal Operations – 25%

Coordinate administrative operations supporting the successful implementation of College Corps.
Interpret and apply university, CSU, California Volunteers, AmeriCorps, and grant policies and requirements.
Coordinate eligibility verification, background check processes, MyAmeriCorps enrollment, America Learns documentation, and other participant requirements.
Maintain accurate participant records and program databases and monitor service hours, living allowance eligibility, education award eligibility, and supporting documentation.
Track and reconcile program expenditures, purchasing transactions, reimbursements, P-Card activity, and other fiscal records.
Maintain financial, procurement, and administrative documentation supporting grant reporting, audits, and compliance.

Communications, Outreach & Program Promotion – 10%

Develop communications for Fellows, community partners, campus stakeholders, and prospective applicants.
Coordinate recruitment campaigns across print, digital, and social media channels.
Create presentations, newsletters, webpages, graphics, marketing materials, and other resources that promote College Corps.
Represent ICCE and College Corps at recruitment fairs, campus events, conferences, presentations, and community outreach activities.

Assessment, Events & Continuous Improvement – 10%

Coordinate orientations, trainings, leadership programs, partner meetings, retreats, networking opportunities, recognition programs, and special events.
Collect and analyze program data to support assessment, grant reporting, and evaluation.
Develop reports, surveys, dashboards, and recommendations that help strengthen program effectiveness and the participant experience.
Identify opportunities to improve operations and contribute to strategic planning and new initiatives.

Approximately 5% of the position will support other duties and institute priorities as assigned.

Experience You Will Bring

A bachelor’s degree and/or equivalent training and administrative work experience involving analysis, evaluation, and the development or improvement of programs, practices, policies, or procedures.
Experience independently planning, organizing, coordinating, and completing administrative or program-related work.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and projects while exercising sound judgment and initiative.
Experience collecting, evaluating, and interpreting information and data to develop recommendations and improve programs.
Working knowledge of operational and fiscal analysis and administrative practices.
Ability to interpret policies, procedures, and regulations and translate them into effective program operations.
Strong written, verbal, presentation, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to collaborate effectively with students, faculty, staff, community organizations, and other internal and external stakeholders.
Ability to anticipate challenges, develop solutions, and proactively address program needs.
Commitment to collaboration, client service, inclusion, and creating a supportive environment for people from diverse backgrounds.

Experience with AmeriCorps, California College Corps, grant-funded service programs, civic engagement, experiential learning, higher education, cohort-based programming, community partnerships, participant data systems, educational programming, or outreach and communications is especially valuable.

This position is designated as a mandated reporter under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and must comply with CSU Executive Order 1083 as a condition of employment. A background check is also required. Occasional evening and/or weekend work and travel between campus and community partner locations may be necessary. The position includes occasional lifting and moving of event and outreach materials weighing up to 20 pounds.

What’s in it for you:

The anticipated annual salary for this position is $63,000 – $64,000
.
This position requires onsite presence on campus 5 days/week but allows for a flexible schedule to attend fun events to get the word out about the program!

new_jobs.title: PSO Program Manager, Community Connect
new_jobs.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.
At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact
Axon Community Connect enables public safety agencies to build voluntary, policy-based partnerships with businesses and community members. Through camera registration and secure camera integration, the program expands investigative reach and real-time situational awareness during critical incidents while maintaining privacy, transparency, and camera-owner control.
As the PSO Program Manager, Community Connect, you will lead the operational health and scalable execution of the Community Connect program across Axon’s U.S. customer base and growing international footprint.
You will establish the operating discipline that enables Program Coordinators to deliver consistent agency outcomes. This includes maintaining visibility into program performance, work-order health, delivery dependencies, technical readiness, and customer-impacting risks; strengthening the processes, tools, and playbooks used across the team; and ensuring complex issues receive the appropriate cross-functional attention.
You will serve as a program-level escalation resource, coordinating with Professional Services, Product, Engineering, Support, Sales, and Finance to remove blockers and drive resolution. You will also provide consultative support for hardware deployment readiness, remote hardware configuration and activation, connectivity, and camera integration requirements.
Your work will enable agencies to launch and sustain Community Connect programs that extend operational visibility, strengthen community participation, and scale responsibly without compromising privacy or the customer experience.
What You’ll Do
Location:
Remote - PT or MT Time Zones 
Travel:
Approximately 30%
Reports to:
Manager, Program Management (Community Connect)
Partner with PSO leadership to implement scalable workflows, operating rhythms, documentation, and reporting that support consistent program delivery.
Maintain visibility into overall program performance, project status, delivery milestones, dependencies, and customer-impacting risks.
Coordinate with Product, Engineering, Support, Sales, Finance, and other internal teams to remove delivery blockers, manage escalations, and improve the customer experience.
Support work-order management and closure activities, including quality checks, documentation, and internal handoffs.
Serve as a technical resource for deployment planning, hardware readiness, network connectivity, configuration, and integration requirements.
Support the deployment of Cores placed in the field by Community Connect team members, including remote configuration, activation, validation, and onsite technical support when needed.
Troubleshoot hardware, network, connectivity, and video-integration issues; document findings and coordinate escalation with the appropriate technical resources to drive resolution.
Create and maintain technical readiness guidance, deployment checklists, troubleshooting resources, and escalation paths for common Community Connect deployment scenarios.
Develop and maintain playbooks, training materials, job aids, and knowledge resources that enable consistent team execution.
Identify recurring delivery, technical, and process issues; partner with leadership to implement improvements that strengthen program execution at scale.
Support adoption of new products, internal tools, and program updates by ensuring the team has clear guidance and readiness resources.

What You Bring
Bachelor’s degree in program management, project management, operations, information technology, professional services, or a related field; or equivalent practical experience, including 2+ years supporting customer-facing technical deployments, implementations, or professional-services programs involving remote hardware configuration, activation, troubleshooting, and field deployment coordination.
Working knowledge of hardware, networking, connectivity, and integration concepts—including IP addressing, DHCP, DNS, VLANs, firewalls, ports, Wi-Fi, bandwidth, and basic troubleshooting—and the ability to translate technical findings into clear next steps.
Experience managing complex, customer-facing work involving multiple stakeholders, dependencies, risks, competing priorities, and technical escalations.
Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to maintain clear documentation, coordinate across teams, and drive issues through resolution.
Experience developing and improving workflows, playbooks, technical guidance, training materials, and knowledge resources that enable consistent execution.
Proficiency with CRM, project-management, and workflow tools such as Salesforce, Smartsheet, Jira, or similar platforms, as well as Microsoft Office and Google Workspace.
Analytical mindset, with the ability to use data and feedback to identify trends, surface risks, and improve operational performance.
Experience in public safety, SaaS, video technology, physical security technology, connected hardware, or a comparable technical environment is preferred.
Must pass a Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) background check and maintain CJIS clearance.
Ability to handle confidential and highly sensitive information with discretion and sound judgment.

Benefits that Benefit You
Competitive salary and 401k with employer match
Discretionary paid time off
Paid parental leave for all
Medical, Dental, Vision plans
Fitness Programs
Emotional & Mental Wellness support
Learning & Development programs
Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)
And yes, we have snacks in our offices

Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work.

Axon is a total compensation company, meaning compensation is made up of base pay, bonus, and stock awards. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: level, function, training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs, geographic market, and often a combination of all these factors. Our benefits offer an array of options to help support you physically, financially and emotionally through the big milestones and in your everyday life. To see more details on our benefits offerings please visit https://www.axon.com/careers.
Base Pay Range: $68,100 USD - $108,960 USD
Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.
Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
Important Notes

The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions.
Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment.
We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at  axongreenhousesupport@axon.com
 or via our Axon Privacy Web Form. For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice.
Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment.

new_jobs.description:
Job Title: Clinical Data Analyst – Medical Imaging

Duration: 6 months with possible extension and conversion into Full time

Location: Remote

Job Description:

Client designs and manufactures state-of-the-art robot-assisted systems for use in minimally invasive surgery.
These systems are revolutionizing the way in which surgery is being done and offer a unique platform—that is being used routinely at hospitals worldwide—for exploring the potential of intelligent surgery.
Joining them means joining a team dedicated to using technology to benefit patients by improving surgical efficacy and decreasing surgical invasiveness, with patient safety as our highest priority.

Responsibilities:

We are seeking a highly motivated Clinical Data Specialist to support the development and validation of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies for robotic-assisted surgery.
The Clinical Data Specialist will create, review, and maintain high-quality clinical ground truth datasets derived from surgical videos, images, and associated clinical information.
This role operates at the intersection of clinical knowledge, data operations, and product development, helping translate clinical and technical requirements into accurate, consistent, and traceable datasets.
The successful candidate will perform clinical annotation and quality review, investigate annotation discrepancies, maintain dataset and methodology documentation, and support the preparation of datasets used for machine learning research, product development, and verification and validation activities.
This individual will collaborate closely with machine learning engineers, researchers, surgeons, clinical experts, quality and regulatory partners, data operations teams, and external annotation providers.
The ideal candidate combines strong knowledge of anatomy and surgical workflows with exceptional attention to detail, documentation discipline, and sound judgment when working with complex or ambiguous clinical data.

Responsibilities:

Review annotations produced by human annotators, clinical experts, external providers, and AI/ML models to ensure accuracy and consistency.
Identify, document, and escalate ambiguous cases, annotation discrepancies, and data-quality risks for clinical review or adjudication.
Participate in annotation training, calibration, qualification, and inter-annotator agreement activities.

Maintain annotation guidelines, quality criteria, review decisions, dataset changes, and other supporting documentation.
Support traceability between source data, annotation versions, quality reviews, adjudication decisions, and approved dataset outputs.
Collaborate with engineers, researchers, surgeons, clinical experts, and external providers to translate clinical data requirements into annotation and review activities.
Contribute to clinical data collection, tool and model evaluation, and workflow improvements that increase efficiency while maintaining clinical accuracy and data quality.
Conduct clinical research through literature review, procedural analysis, and consultation with clinical experts to support AI/ML research and product-development needs.

Technical Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in biology, physiology, biomedical engineering, nursing, clinical sciences, health sciences, or a related field.

Strong understanding of human anatomy and an interest in learning surgical procedures across multiple specialties.

Experience interpreting medical images, surgical videos, clinical workflows, or other complex visual data.

Experience with data annotation, clinical data review, medical research, clinical operations, or a related field.
Ability to learn and use specialized annotation platforms, data-management systems, and project-tracking tools.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to recognize patterns, inconsistencies, and potential data-quality risks.
Demonstrated ability to follow detailed clinical definitions and apply them consistently.
Excellent documentation skills and the ability to clearly explain annotation decisions and clinical reasoning.
Ability to handle confidential, proprietary, and sensitive clinical information professionally.

Soft Skills and Leadership Requirements:

Excellent attention to detail and commitment to clinical accuracy and data quality.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including clear documentation of decisions and concerns.
Ability to collaborate effectively with clinical, technical, operational, and quality-focused stakeholders.
Sound judgment regarding when to make an independent decision and when to escalate a clinical or quality concern.
Ability to translate clinical and AI/ML research objectives into practical data collection, annotation, and quality-review guidelines.

Ability to manage multiple projects, priorities, and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Proactive and transparent in communicating mistakes, uncertainty, risks, and process challenges.
Ability to work independently while remaining closely coordinated with a cross-functional team.
Open to giving and receiving constructive feedback and contributing to continuous improvement.

Title:
Diversion Case Manager

Reports To:
Mental Health Manager

Salary Range:
$41,212.04 - $44,302.94 annually

La Casa Norte’s mission is to serve youth and families confronting homelessness. We provide access to stable housing and deliver comprehensive services that act as a catalyst to transform lives and communities. La Casa Norte’s mission and philosophy of service is to impact the social issues of homelessness at the individual and community levels.

Job Summary

La Casa Norte is seeking a committed and compassionate Diversion Case Manager
to support clients experiencing homelessness or housing instability. This full-time position plays a key role in providing housing-focused case management and diversion services. The role assists youth experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness in maintaining or obtaining stable housing.

Summary Of Responsibilities

Connect with clients referred from the Coordinated Entry system to assess their level of housing instability and their barriers to stable housing. Provide direct assistance through housing navigation, disbursement of homelessness diversion funds and other resources, and referrals to internal mental health services and/or external partners.

Housing Stability and Case Management

Provide intensive, client-centered case management rooted in Harm Reduction and Trauma-Informed Care.
Conduct intake assessments and pre-housing evaluations.
Support clients through housing navigation, lease-up, move-in processes as well as with housing retention.
Attend apartment viewings and other appointments with clients when needed.
Conduct home visits and community-based meetings with clients when needed.
Deliver life skills education on topics such as budgeting, conflict resolution, wellness, and tenant rights.
Facilitate access to medical, legal, mental health, and substance use services through internal and external referrals.
Mediate landlord-tenant issues and support long-term housing retention.
Provide coaching on tenancy expectations, budgeting, and independent living skills.
Assist clients in obtaining vital documents like ID, Social Security card, birth certificate, etc.
Administer financial assistance for rent, security deposits, and utilities when applicable.

Client Support

Use motivational interviewing, client centered care, and a strengths-based perspective to promote positive behavioral change.
Work collaboratively with clients to develop tailored service plans, outlining clear goals and tasks towards housing stability and financial self-sufficiency.
Provide counseling and mentorship.
Advocate for clients at landlord/tenant court and other legal settings when necessary.
Address systemic barriers to housing access.
Advocate for clients with public institutions (IDHS, Social Security, schools, etc.).
Connect clients to LCN programs and external services, including mental health, food, clothing, employment, education, and benefits.
Support income growth through employment services or benefits enrollment.
Educate clients on financial tools, credit repair, and responsible financial management.

Compliance, Reporting, & Organizational Participation

Maintain timely and accurate case notes and documentation using Homeless Management Information System (HMIS), ClientTrack, Caseworthy, and/or other databases.
Ensure paperwork is completed in an accurate, consistent, and timely manner.
Monitor client progress toward service plan goals and adjust as needed.
Participate in on-call rotation and provide crisis intervention as required.
Attend weekly staff meetings and other staff trainings.
Participate in La Casa Norte’s fundraising events as needed.
Assist with data collection and completion of program reports.
Perform other duties as required.

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor’s degree in social work, psychology, or a related field or at least three (3) years of equivalent experience.
Knowledge of and familiarity with family systems.
Prior experience working with homeless and at-risk populations desired.
Familiarity with Chicago’s housing and human services systems.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to facilitate group sessions.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
Proficient in the use of computers, research tools and database systems.
Valid driver’s license, proof of insurance, and access to a reliable vehicle.

Preferred

Bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred.
Experience in supportive housing, housing navigation, emergency shelter, youth services, or reentry work.
Familiarity with CaseWorthy, HMIS, or other case management systems.

Core Competencies

Commitment to housing justice and client empowerment.
Cultural competency and sensitivity.
Collaborative spirit and strong advocacy skills.
Adaptability in a dynamic service environment.

Job Summary

The Community Health Worker (CHW) will serve as a bridge between under-served communities and the health and social service systems. As a non-clinical role, work within the patient-centered medical home model, which embraces a team approach to chronic disease self-management. Provide information and assistance to help patients navigate a complex health and human services system. Strong advocacy and raising awareness of individual and community health needs are necessary for efficient and culturally sensitive work.

Must strive to build capacity for access to services and community engagement. Strong communication skills from a non-judgmental perspective will be necessary to engage patients in their own care, articulate clearly and effectively when advocating for patients and community groups, and assist members in understanding and effectively navigating complex health systems. Effective active listening skills are essential. Actively engage in relationship building and work from a team-based perspective.

Collaborate on goal setting and care planning within an inter-professional team context. Required to give presentations to community groups, and requires strong public speaking and presentation skills that include diplomacy and tact. Strong organization skills and the ability to anticipate future planning needs is required. Effective coordination skills are necessary in facilitating appointment attendance and individual plans of care. Serves as a point person for issues and related solutions while maintaining appropriate boundaries.

Hold knowledge and experience of ethnic and cultural populations, government partners, community stakeholders, and other organizations. Model effective problem solving skills to empower patients to take an active role in their health care. Must have a thorough understanding of self-efficacy theory and its application when working with others who have chronic disease. Embrace cultural sensitivity when seeking information and working with others.

Documents completion of assigned activities and support of community members as required. Provide services under supervision as directed by state or other regulatory requirements. Strictly adhere to the scope of their duties and will not give medical advice under any circumstance. Strong adherence to all patient privacy laws in health care settings and the community is essential.

High school diploma or equivalent required. College courses strongly preferred but not required.

Preferred qualifications include a minimum of three years of ambulatory care experience, experience in community outreach, and/or working knowledge of various integrated systems of care in the community. Personal experience living with a chronic health condition is preferred.

Motivational Interviewing skills are required with training, to be completed within six months of hire.

Proof of certificate from a Community Health Worker program is required upon hire or within six months.

The primary role for the Data Analyst I is to develop analytical solutions to identify new opportunities, expand existing analytical methods, provide insights, and build practical solutions to complex business challenges. In this role, the Analyst will develop and maintain dashboards in Power BI, conduct trend analyses, and assist in validating key financial and operational datasets. Additionally, the Data Analyst will be tasked with utilizing descriptive analytical strategies to enable leaders to make data-driven insights. The Data Analyst will also collaborate with department leadership to develop tools that support product and profitability growth. Additional responsibilities include importing, validating, and managing datasets from external and internal sources to ensure accuracy and alignment with business needs.

Job Duties And Responsibilities

Data Analysis, Visualization & Management

Build, maintain and enhance Power BI dashboards and reports to support operational decision-making.
Conduct data mining and advanced statistical analysis to provide actionable insights and identify trends to measure and optimize product performance for the business’ top product lines.
Leverage SQL queries for data extraction projects.
Manage carrier file imports and conduct frequent database audits to ensure data integrity.
Conduct root cause analyses to provide actionable insights into an account’s performance.
Communicate and clearly present findings/results to department leadership.

Report Management & Production

Design, distribute, and maintain weekly, monthly, and quarterly product performance reports.
Support the automation of manual reporting processes by creating scalable reporting solutions using Power BI.
Support ad-hoc data and reporting needs for various operational initiatives.
Conduct monthly audit and reconciliations of external data.
Supports the department’s data extraction and collection needs.

Process Improvement

Proactively identify areas for operational efficiencies and collaborate with various business units to provide scalable solutions to increase efficiency.
Collaborate with other data leaders to streamline reporting and provide automated solutions to manually conducted reporting.
Partner with team members to standardize data collection, management, and visualization best practices.

Perform other duties as assigned

Serve as data analysis resource on as needed projects.
Support initiatives focused on enabling a self-service analytics environment.

Qualifications (Education, Experience, Certifications & KSA)

Associate’s degree in a related field required.
Bachelor’s degree in mathematics, statistics or computer science, or 6+ years equivalent experience preferred.
1-2 years of work-related experience required.
Proficiency in core Microsoft packages required (Word, Excel and PowerPoint) required.
Foundational experience building and maintaining reports and dashboards in Power BI required (or other BI tools with willingness to learn Power BI quickly).
Experience with SQL or other SAS languages preferred but not required.
Strong analytical skills with an ability to translate data findings into meaningful business insights.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, skills, efforts or working conditions associated with a job.

Our diverse business portfolio allows employees broad career options with the advantage of staying with the same organization.

new_jobs.title: RN Case Manager Full Time
new_jobs.description:
Overview

JOB SUMMARY

Directs and coordinates the integration of Case Management functions into the patient care, discharge, and home planning processes with other hospital departments, external service organizations, agencies, and health care facilities.

Responsibilities

SUMMARY OF ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Provide care for the Adult or Geriatric patient, ages 18 years and over.
Demonstrates and understands the importance of and respect for the rights, dignity and individuality of each patient in all interactions.
Coordinates the provision of clinical care to patients, families and significant others to enable them to deal with the impact of illness on individual family functioning and to achieve maximum benefits from health care services.
Complete psychosocial assessment on all new admissions based on hospital policy and procedures within three business days.
Develop and is involved in the implementation of programs to assist patients and their families with the social and psychological factors of illness.
Develop with physicians, nursing personnel, and other members of the management team in the planning of patient care services and the patient care plan.
Engage in individual or group intervention sessions pertaining to care and adjustment.
Arrange for discharge and post-hospital care of patents through institutions and agencies within the community.
Provide advice and guidance in handling special cases or patient needs.
Coordinate the provision of information and guidance to patients, their families, and other hospital departments regarding all aspects of patients’ post-discharge treatment and recovery programs.
Coordinate the referral of patients and families to appropriate community, social service, home health services, extended care, and rehabilitation facilities and organizations.
Coordinate Case Management communications to ensure the staff’s awareness of available services and resources; serves as the primary liaison with external social service organizations.
Participate in the coordination of interdepartmental program planning and implementation efforts, and support related projects and activities.
Participate in the Case Management educational programs for physicians and other departments to enhance their understanding of medical necessity aspects of health care delivery.
Represent the department on various hospital committees.
Develop and implement Pastoral Care Program in conjunction with Pastoral Care from Host hospital.
Develop and maintain harmonious working relationships with other departments; address interdepartmental social service issues.
Assist in the preparation of and monitor the department budget in compliance with established budgeting procedures. Identify and respond to variances. Case Management monitors Utilization reviews and patients LOS.
Direct the quality improvement activities for the department and promotes the maintenance of high-quality, safe and effective patient care.
Prepare statistical reports on department services and patient needs.

Standard Job Duties

Adheres to all components of the Hospital Compliance Plan in performing job duties and reports any violations or suspected violations of the Plan to the Compliance Officer.
Demonstrates professional conduct and complies with hospital and departmental policies and procedures.
Adheres to hospital attendance policy as outlined in the Employee Handbook.
Complies with measures for preventing exposure to blood borne pathogens.
Participates in the Hazardous Material Program; hazards include exposure to blood and body fluids, possible communicable diseases, sharp objects and instruments, assorted chemicals and gases as listed in the Hazardous Materials Program Manual.
Complies with established Safety and Patient Safety Program practices.
Performs other incidental and related duties, as required and/or assigned.
Develops an understanding of responsibilities for recognizing patient abuse and follows policy for making appropriate referrals/interventions.
Develops an understanding of responsibilities for participation in Performance Improvement activities and participates in such activities.
Limits access to protected health information (PHI) to the information reasonably necessary to do the job, and shares such information only on a need-to-know basis for work purposes.

(Access to verbal, written and electronic PHI for this job has been determined based on job level and job responsibility within the organization. Computerized access to PHI for this job has been determined as described above and is controlled via user ID and password.)

Qualifications

Qualifications:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.

The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education/Experience

Bachelor's degree in a healthcare related field, social service field, or RN. Two years’ Healthcare/Hospital experience as RN or Social Worker preferred.

Computer Skills

Knowledge of basic computer skills and word processing.

Certificates And Licenses

Licensed as a Registered Nurse or Social Worker in state of employment. Must obtain BLS within 30 days of employment and maintain for the duration of employment.

Supervisory Responsibilities

None

Work Environment

The work environment is representative of that which an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Physical Demands

The physical demands of this job are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodation may be made to a qualified individual with a disability who can perform the essential functions of this position with or without reasonable accommodation. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus while performing the duties of this job. The employee is regularly required to stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; talk; and hear.

Acknowledgement Of Receipt And Acceptance Of Job Description

Job Description

BenchMark Physical Therapy, a brand partner of Upstream Rehabilitation, is looking for a Patient Care Coordinator to join our team in Maynardville, TN

Are you looking for a position in a growing organization where you can make a significant impact on the lives of others?

What is a Patient Care Coordinator?

A Patient Care Coordinator is an entry-level office role that is responsible for maintaining pleasant and consistent daily operations of the clinic.
Our Patient Care Coordinators have excellent customer service skills.
Patient Care Coordinators learn new things – a lot! The Patient Care Coordinator multitasks in multiple computer programs each day.

A day in the life of a Patient Care Coordinator:

Greets everyone who enters the clinic in a friendly and welcoming manner.
Schedules new referrals received by fax or by telephone from patients, physician offices.
Verifies insurance coverage for patients.
Collects patient payments.
Maintains an orderly and organized front office workspace.
Other duties as assigned.

Fulltime positions include:

Annual paid Charity Day to give back to a cause meaningful to you
Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Insurance
3-week Paid Time Off plus paid holidays
401K + company match

Position Summary:

The Patient Care Coordinator - I (PCC-I) supports clinic growth through excellence in execution of the practice management role and patient intake processes. This individual will work in collaboration with the Clinic Director (CD) to carry out efficient clinic procedures. The PCC-I position is responsible for supporting the mission, vision, and values of Upstream Rehabilitation.

Responsibilities:

Core responsibilities
Collect all money due at the time of service
Convert referrals into evaluations
Schedule patient visits
Customer Service

Create an inviting clinic atmosphere.
Make all welcome calls
Monitor and influence arrival rate through creation of a great customer experience

Practice Management
Manage schedule efficiently
Manage document routing
Manage personal overtime
Manage non-clinical documentation
Manage deposits
Manage caseload, D/C candidate, progress note, and insurance reporting
Monitor clinic inventory

Complete quarterly compliance training.

Ability to multitask, organizational detail, ability to meet deadlines, work with little to no supervision
As a member of a team, must possess efficient time management and presentation skills

Description

Work hard, have fun, make history. That's what we do every day at Amazon. As a key leader within Amazon's Global Real Estate & Facilities (GREF) team, the Space Program Manager will own the end-to-end space allocation strategy for their assigned Finance Operations business units, driving results by managing complex programs across multiple stakeholders with competing priorities and tight timelines.

The Space Program Manager will take full ownership of aligning real estate strategy to business needs in partnership with key GREF stakeholders while maintaining a customer-centric approach. This role requires strong program management discipline: structuring multi-workstream initiatives, managing dependencies and trade-offs, and delivering on commitments in a fast-paced environment where requirements shift rapidly. The role will partner with managers, occupancy planning teams, and space management teams to implement workplace design, space, and move needs for their assigned team(s), in order to inform supply and demand allocations and change requests.

The Space Program Manager will be responsible for developing strategic recommendations to managers regarding their workplace design and space allocation, and translating them into GREF's broader business requirements that enable effective solutions in alignment with Amazon's overall workplace strategy.

The ideal candidate demonstrates ownership — proactively identifying gaps, driving solutions, and delivering outcomes without waiting for direction. They bring a bias for action — making high-quality decisions quickly with available data, taking calculated risks, and iterating rather than waiting for perfect information. They bring strong stakeholder management capability: navigating conflicting needs across multiple business units, building trust through transparency and data, and influencing outcomes at varied levels of the organization. They approach planning with rigor — developing structured programs with clear milestones, tracking progress against metrics, and proactively mitigating risks. The candidate must be comfortable operating in ambiguity, escalating appropriately, and delivering results in incomplete-information environments.

Key job responsibilities

Own end-to-end space allocation and program delivery for assigned Finance business units — from requirements gathering through execution and stakeholder communication
Drive collaboration with business unit leaders to understand their real estate and portfolio needs, ensuring requirements are accurately captured, prioritized, and addressed on timeline
Manage cross-functional coordination with Amazon Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Finance Leaders, Global Business Partnering (GBP) and Human Resources to validate headcount data (i.e., forecasted demand), proactively resolving discrepancies
Own the end-to-end business-related deliverables for move projects, including origin lists, move notifications, destination lists, and other related tasks — managing these as structured programs with clear milestones and accountability
Deliver defect resolution related to space allocation by identifying root causes, implementing fixes, and driving prevention mechanisms
Maintain clear and consistent communication with business units, providing proactive updates and managing stakeholder expectations through data-driven reporting
Identify and implement process improvements in move and space management operations — measuring impact, scaling what works, and raising the bar on efficiency
Navigate a matrix reporting structure encompassing both dotted and hard reporting lines, influencing without authority and aligning competing priorities across organizational boundaries

A day in the life

This role blends data validation, stakeholder collaboration, and program execution. You validate headcount data, analyze space requirements, and deliver allocation recommendations while collaborating daily with RPM, GBP, SPOCs, Occupancy Planning, and MAC teams — serving as the connective tissue between these partners and the leaders you support. Work ranges from routine onboarding coordination to complex restacks with competing priorities and hard deadlines. You are heavily customer-facing, own monthly and quarterly business reporting that informs leadership decisions, and drive strategic alignment through data transparency and proactive communication.

About The Team

This role sits within AMER Regional Portfolio Management (RPM), reporting through the larger Occupancy Planning organization. The team structure provides built-in partnerships with Occupancy Planning, Global Business Partnering, MAC, and SPOCs — giving the new hire a strong framework to ramp quickly. The Space Program Manager directly supports Finance Operations leaders as their primary customer and stakeholder, translating business needs into space outcomes. This is a dynamic, cross-functional team that indexes strong on Ownership, Deliver Results, and Earn Trust — we move fast, take accountability, and build credibility through consistent execution.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project management experience, or a Bachelor's degree and 3+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience working cross-functionally with tech and non-tech teams
Experience with one or more analytics visualization tools (e.g., Excel, Tableau, QuickSight, MicroStrategy, PowerBI)

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
Experience working and contributing to project playbooks, building schedules, managing issues/risks, establishing communication plans and stakeholder management
Experience prioritizing competing demands, scoping large efforts, and negotiating timelines

new_jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

We are HALO! We connect people and brands to create unforgettable, meaningful, and lasting experiences that build brand engagement and loyalty for our over 60,000 clients globally. Our nearly 2,000 employees and 1,000 Account Executives located in 40+ sales offices across the United States are the reason HALO is the global leader in branded merchandise, uniform programs, and recognition and incentive solutions.

HALO is seeking an External Workforce & BPO Program Manager
to lead and evolve our contingent workforce and outsourced services programs. This role serves as the primary owner of the processes, partnerships, and operational controls that support our global non-employee workforce, including domestic and global temporary labor, as well as agency and BPO partners.

The ideal candidate is equally comfortable developing workforce strategies and executive-level partnerships as they are maintaining accurate records, tracking headcount, generating reports and insights, auditing data, and ensuring operational excellence. This role requires a hands-on, detail-oriented professional who thrives in building structure, creating scalable processes, managing vendor relationships, and driving business outcomes across a complex global workforce environment.

Duties & Responsibilities

Stakeholder Consultation & Workforce Planning

Serve as a trusted advisor to Talent Acquisition, Human Resources, Finance, and business leaders regarding contingent labor and outsourced workforce strategies.
Consult with business stakeholders on talent fulfillment options, including employee, contingent labor, project-based resources, and BPO solutions.
Provide data-driven insights and recommendations to HRBPs, Talent Acquisition, Finance, and business leaders on the optimal talent fulfillment approach, working to understand workforce needs and develop scalable, cost-effective staffing solutions.
Build strong working relationships across functions to ensure alignment, transparency, and effective decision-making.
Partner with Finance and business stakeholders to support workforce planning, budget forecasting, labor cost analysis, and spend reporting associated with contingent workforce and outsourced labor programs.

Program Creation & System Administration

Own the day-to-day administration of contingent workforce records, tracking systems, vendor rosters, contracts, and reporting tools to ensure accuracy and visibility across the organization.
Maintain a high degree of data integrity through regular audits, reconciliations, reporting reviews, and process documentation.
Establish and continuously improve processes that create structure, accountability, and scalability as the program evolves.
Reconcile and process invoices associated with agencies, ensuring accuracy against approved contracts, rates, and SOWs
Investigate and resolve invoice discrepancies, payment issues, and vendor inquiries.

Contingent Workforce Program Governance

Lead cross-functional collaboration with business leaders, Talent Acquisition, Human Resources, Finance, and Legal to assess workforce solution providers, staffing partners, and contingent labor vendors.
Direct operational lifecycle workflows of domestic and global contract talent, ensuring successful implementation through established governance, contracting, risk management, onboarding and offboarding processes.
Partner with HRBPs and TA to create guidelines for how and when hiring needs are released to secondary or tertiary staffing agencies.
Ensure QBRs are conducted to assess optimization, program savings, SLA, and other agreed-upon metrics.
Track contract renewals, fee structures, volume discount tiers built into various agreements.

BPO Relationship & Vendor Management

Develop trusted, collaborative relationships with external partners locally and globally while holding vendors accountable for performance, service delivery, compliance, and business outcomes.
Influence vendor behavior through partnership, performance management, and continuous improvement initiatives rather than solely through contractual enforcement.
Serve as the primary point of contact to investigate and resolve third-party delivery bottlenecks, performance lags, or cross-border vendor staffing issues.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree preferred.
6+ years of experience in contingent workforce management, workforce programs, talent acquisition operations, vendor management, HR operations, procurement, program management, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience managing programs that require both strategic stakeholder consultation and detailed operational execution.
Proven ability to establish, document, and continuously improve processes while maintaining data integrity, operational controls, and program consistency in evolving environments.
Experience evaluating workforce fulfillment models and advising stakeholders on employee, contingent labor, project-based, and outsourced workforce solutions.
Strong relationship management and influencing skills with the ability to effectively partner with business leaders, Talent Acquisition, Human Resources, Finance, Legal, vendors, and other cross-functional stakeholders.
Prior success migrating a corporate entity from manual spreadsheet-based vendor tracking to a formal Vendor Management System (VMS) strongly preferred.
Certification in Contingent Workforce Management (CCWP) or project management principles (PMP) strongly preferred.

Compensation:
The estimated base salary range for this position is between $95,000 and $110,000 annually. Please note that this pay range serves as a general guideline and reflects a broad spectrum of labor markets across the US. While it is uncommon for candidates to be hired at or near the top of the range, compensation decisions are influenced by various factors. At HALO, these include, but are not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the role, the candidate's work experience, location, education and training, key skills, internal equity, external market data, and broader market and business considerations.

Benefits:
At HALO, we offer benefits that support all aspects of your life, helping you find a work-life balance that’s right for you. Our comprehensive benefits include nationwide coverage for Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, and Disability insurance, along with additional Voluntary Benefits. Prepare for your financial future with our 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan, Health Savings Accounts (HSA), and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA).

Application Information:
To apply to this opportunity, click the APPLY button at the top right or very bottom of the screen to complete our online application. A resume is optional, so you may choose to upload and have the application prefill with your information. There are 5 sections to complete in total, including General information, Work History, Education, Compliance, and optional demographic questions. Once you have successfully submitted your application, you will receive a submission confirmation email from our system.

Application Deadline:
Applications are reviewed and processed only when there is a specific need or opportunity, rather than on a fixed schedule or at a set deadline. Because they are reviewed on an as-needed basis, a job posting will be removed once the position has been filled or is no longer available.

More About HALO

At HALO, we unleash the energy of our client's brands and amplify their stories to capture the attention of those who matter most. For that reason, more than 60,000 small- and mid-sized businesses work with HALO and have made us the global leader of the branded merchandise industry.

Career Advancement: At HALO, we love promoting from within. Internal promotions have been the key to our exponential growth in the last few years. With so many industry leaders at HALO, you'll have the opportunity to accelerate your career by learning from their experience, insights, and skills and gain access to HALO's influential global network, leadership experiences, and diverse thinking.
Culture: We love working here and know that you will too. You can expect a positive culture of ingenuity, inclusion, and relentless determination. We push the limits of possibilities and imagination by staying curious, humble, and provocative in order to break through yesterday's limit. Diversity is the source of our creativity and we thrive when each of us contributes to an inclusive culture of respect, dignity, and equity mindset in everything we do. We keep our promise for excellence with an unrelenting commitment to achieving results and supporting one another to stay accountable, transparent, and dependable.
Recognition: You're going to succeed here, and you can count on us to celebrate your wins. Colleagues across the company will join in recognizing your big milestones and nominate you for awards. Over time, you'll earn so much recognition that you can convert into gift cards, trips, concerts, and merchandise at your favorite brands.
Flexibility: Most roles offer hybrid work. In addition, we pride ourselves on flexible schedules that help you find a balance between professional and personal demands. We believe that supporting our customers is the priority and trust that you and your manager will find a schedule to achieve that priority.

HALO is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We insist on an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy (including childbirth, lactation and related medical conditions), national origin, age, physical and mental disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information (including characteristics and testing), military and veteran status, and any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Company Description
The Town of Cheraw, South Carolina, is one of the state’s oldest and most scenic inland communities, known for its historic charm and natural beauty. Named for the Cheraw Indians, the town began as a small trading post at the head of navigation on the Great Pee Dee River. Its wide streets and town green, laid out in the 18th century, now form the heart of the 213-acre Cheraw Historic District on the National Register of Historic Places. The area is rich with gardens, parks, and architecture that reflect more than 200 years of history. Cheraw offers a welcoming environment that values community, recreation, and preservation of its cultural heritage.
Role Description
The Youth Sports Program Coordinator is a full-time, on-site role located in Cheraw, SC, responsible for planning, organizing, and overseeing youth sports programs and activities. This position coordinates seasonal leagues, clinics, and special events, including scheduling practices and games, securing facilities and equipment, and communicating with participants, families, coaches, and officials. The coordinator develops program guidelines, ensures a safe and inclusive environment, and promotes positive sportsmanship and skill development for young participants. Daily tasks include program administration, registration management, budget tracking, and collaboration with town staff and community partners to grow participation. The role also involves evaluating program effectiveness, maintaining records, and assisting with marketing and outreach efforts to promote youth sports offerings.
Qualifications

Experience coordinating or coaching youth sports programs, leagues, or recreational activities.
Skills in event and program planning, scheduling, and basic budget management.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills for working with youth, families, coaches, and community partners.
Ability to promote a safe, inclusive, and positive environment that supports youth development and sportsmanship.
Organizational and time-management skills, including attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple programs.
Ability to work on-site, including occasional evenings and weekends as programs and events require.
Knowledge of safety practices and risk management in youth sports settings.
High school diploma or equivalent required; coursework or a degree in recreation, sports management, education, or a related field is preferred.
Previous experience in municipal recreation, community programs, or similar public sector roles is a plus.
Ability to pass any required background checks and meet town employment standards.

Department:

Schedule

Full Time, Day Shift (80 hours biweekly)

General Summary

Establishes trusting relationships with identified disparate population groups that strengthens the patient-provider relationship and improves patient care. In addition, disseminates health information in a culturally relevant manner and builds individual and community capacity to address health care needs.

Responsibilities

Essential Functions:

Assesses needs of population, patient or individual on an ongoing basis. Identifies barriers to care and makes appropriate recommendations for follow-up or referral.
Educates community members, either individually or in groups, about how to access and/or use the health care system. Shares relevant concerns from community members with medical providers or others within the health care system.
Identifies and utilizes culturally appropriate outreach strategies to provide specific health promotion and disease prevention education to specific population groups. This may include, but is not limited to: developing and coordinating a network of community lay leaders; implementing community education and screening events, and; conducting relevant follow-up with participants.
Assists, as requested, in the coordination of care for clients/patients. This may include, but is not limited to: facilitating enrollment in public health insurance and charity care; conducting site visits with at-risk patients/clients, and; providing a cultural context for effective medical care and behavior change as part of a clinical care team.

new_jobs.description:
Description

*This role has the potential to sit in any US location*

Amazon's Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) organization is responsible for keeping the material handling equipment, robotics systems, and building infrastructure across our fulfillment network running safely and efficiently. We are a team of technicians, engineers, and program leaders who ensure our operational technology performs at the highest levels - directly enabling Amazon to deliver on its customer promise.

RME is undergoing a transformation from reactive to proactive maintenance strategies across the network. This role is central to that evolution - you'll drive the systems, standards, and data-driven programs that enable our shift toward predictive maintenance and operational excellence at scale.

As a Senior RME Program Manager, you will own the strategy and execution of our Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) programs across the North American fulfillment network. You'll be the network-level SME responsible for driving standardization, improving PM effectiveness, and enabling local teams with the tools, training, and processes they need to maintain world-class equipment reliability.

Key job responsibilities

Be a network level Subject Matter Expert (SME) on the CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System), train and assist the local Reliability Maintenance Engineering Planner and support network initiatives.
Drive RME standards roll-out in North America initiatives and participate in network led projects.
Be a CMMS key user and drive programs to roll out new functionality, procedures, scheduling or reports. Monitor standards implementation through reporting and audits.
Analyze and improve forecasting of preventative maintenance routines to make equipment maintenance less intrusive and more effective.
Compile equipment information, performance metrics and machine histories and make recommendations for improvements based on their findings to the entire network.
Work with the Global Reliability Maintenance Engineering network and initiatives on cost reduction and process improvement for spare parts management, equipment maintenance and maintenance routines.
Ability to Travel up to 50%

A day in the life

As a Senior RME Planner, no two days look the same. You might start your morning reviewing CMMS dashboards and maintenance reports, identifying trends or gaps in preventative maintenance compliance across the network. By mid-morning, you could be leading a training session with local RME Planners on new CMMS functionality or updated scheduling procedures. Afternoons often involve cross-functional collaboration — partnering with site maintenance teams to analyze equipment performance data, working with Global RME stakeholders on spare parts optimization, or presenting program updates and recommendations to senior leadership. You'll balance hands-on system work (building reports, refining PM routines, auditing standards adoption) with strategic thinking about how to make maintenance across the network more efficient and less intrusive. When you're traveling to sites, you'll be on the ground conducting audits, gathering feedback, and coaching local teams. This role sits at the intersection of technology, data, and operations — ideal for someone who loves solving complex problems at scale.

Join the HJF Team!

HJF is seeking a Research Assistant I
to perform research and/or development in collaboration with others. This is the first of four levels within the Research Assistant series.

This position will be in support of the NeuroTrauma Department’s Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) research program, within the Operational Undersea Medicine Directorate (OUMD), located at the Naval Medical Research Center (NMRC) in Silver Spring, MD. HJF provides scientific, technical, and programmatic support services to OUMD.

The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals.

Responsibilities

Participate in in vivo and basic laboratory procedures.
Assist with/or perform surgical, behavioral and other experimental procedures in pre-clinical animal models in support of neurotrauma research - in particular impact and blast-induced traumatic brain injury (TBI).
Assist with/or perform operation of a blast shock tube.
Perform real-time data acquisition using available technologies. This includes measurement of pressure profiles of blast generated by the shock tube, and continuous and automated as well as discrete monitoring of physiological parameters. The incumbent should be comfortable with operating and maintaining data acquisition programs
Assist with/or perform laboratory procedures including biospecimen collection and preparation, Western blots, ELISA, histology, etc.
Assist with maintaining databases. Perform data entry for research projects ensuring that data is entered for analysis in a timely and efficient manner. Ensure that the confidentiality and security of data are maintained.
Assist with data analysis and presentation.
Assist with preparation of standard operating procedures, maintenance of laboratory records, and general upkeep of lab spaces.
Laboratory management responsibilities include routine maintenance of laboratory equipment; managing scheduling of commonly used spaces/equipment; and compliance with departmental and institutional policies.

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in biology, neuroscience, or a relevant field.

The incumbent should have a general working knowledge of good laboratory practices.
They should be comfortable with handling animals and working in animal and laboratory environment.
Excellent time management and self-motivated.
Must be proficient in using Microsoft Word, Excel, Power Point, and is expected to have a working knowledge of statistical analysis and image analysis programs.
For application of specialized programs, the incumbent will be provided required training.
Must be able to work in a team as well as independently.
This position requires that you obtain and maintain a T1/Public Trust background check.
US citizenship is required.

Long periods of standing and sitting; intricate work with hands; handling specimens and various chemicals.

Work Environment

Laboratory environment; may involve working with biohazards; may require working evenings and weekends.

new_jobs.description:
Description

Leidos is seeking a Investigative Data Analyst to support data-driven decision-making by collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and presenting complex information to identify trends, risks, vulnerabilities, and operational insights. This role combines advanced analytical skills, investigative research, quality assurance auditing, and executive-level communication to support organizational leadership. The ideal candidate is a self-motivated professional who excels in working with large datasets, developing meaningful visualizations, and translating technical findings into actionable recommendations.

The Investigative Data Analyst will be a hybrid role, 50% onsite in the Fort Worth, TX office and 50% remote. The candidate for this role must be within commutable distance to the office location.
This position will start as a part-time role with expectation of moving to full time status in January of 2027.

Primary Responsibilities

Analyze complex datasets to identify trends, gaps, anomalies, risks, and potential integrity concerns through statistical and analytical modeling techniques.
Develop and maintain dashboards, reports, charts, graphs, and other visual products using Microsoft Excel, Power BI, and other analytical tools to communicate findings effectively.
Conduct research using government databases, internal data systems, and open-source intelligence (OSINT) resources to support investigations, operational assessments, and strategic initiatives.
Prepare executive summaries, investigative reports, briefing materials, status reports, and presentations for senior leadership, including executive and Congressional stakeholders.
Perform quality assurance reviews and audits of work products, closed cases, management inquiries, and operational processes to ensure compliance with established policies and standards.
Identify emerging trends, systemic vulnerabilities, and operational risks by connecting information across multiple data sources and organizational functions.
Translate complex technical analyses into clear, concise, and actionable recommendations tailored to audiences ranging from technical staff to executive leadership.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, program managers, analysts, investigators, and organizational leadership to support strategic initiatives and operational objectives.
Independently manage assigned projects, establish priorities, monitor timelines, and deliver high-quality work with minimal supervision.
Exercise sound judgment when evaluating sensitive information, recognizing anomalies, and determining when issues require escalation to management.
Support continuous process improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to enhance data quality, reporting capabilities, and operational efficiency.
Ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and appropriate handling of sensitive or restricted information.

Basic Qualifications

Citizenship: U.S. Citizenship required
Clearance: Secret clearance or ability to obtain one
Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Statistics, Criminal Justice, Public Administration, or a related field and 2 years of relevant experieince. Equivalent professional experience may be considered.
Experience analyzing large and complex datasets to identify trends, risks, gaps, and operational insights.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including pivot tables, advanced formulas, data modeling, and analytical functions.
Demonstrated expertise using Microsoft Power BI to create dashboards, visualizations, and interactive reports.
Experience working with databases, government information systems, or other enterprise data repositories.
Knowledge of open-source intelligence (OSINT) research methodologies and publicly available information sources.
Strong technical writing skills with the ability to produce executive summaries, investigative reports, briefing documents, and formal correspondence.
Experience conducting quality assurance reviews, compliance audits, or performance evaluations.
Exceptional analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities with strong pattern recognition skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Proven ability to collaborate effectively across multiple organizational levels and functional areas.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize multiple assignments and meet deadlines while working independently.
Demonstrated professionalism, integrity, discretion, and sound judgment when handling sensitive information.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting federal government agencies or regulatory organizations.
Familiarity with aviation, transportation, law enforcement, inspections, investigations, or regulatory compliance programs.
Experience with SQL, Python, R, or other analytical programming languages.
Knowledge of data governance, data quality management, and business intelligence best practices.
Experience with automated reporting tools, workflow applications, or enterprise case management systems.
Experience preparing executive-level briefings for senior government officials.
